newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's BUX jumps to new record, bucks Euro mkts.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's BUX jumps to new record, bucks Euro mkts.

text.p: The Hungarian share market bucked the falling trend on European markets, anxious ahead of the second round of French elections, and rallied to a new record high on Friday, causing some surprise, traders said.
"Friday's rise caused surprise, people expected a calm session," said Robert Forgo of MKB Securities.
The BUX index finished at 6,018.11 points, up 88.96 points or 1.50 percent, after a slow start.
Traders attributed the sudden rise to inflow of fresh funds to the Budapest bourse, which seems to be one of the new destinations of money leaving the troubled Czech markets.

"Money suddenly started to flow in from abroad," Forgo said, adding the steam drove the BUX index over the 6,000 point level for the first time by close. Earlier this week the indicator rose to a trading high of 6,012.20 points.
"Money shifts over to Hungary because of problems on the Czech markets," said Forgo, adding that further reason might be that investors digested the first quarter earnings and now decided to move.

Gyorgy Czipo of ING Barings shared the view that the Budapest bourse provided investment opportunities for funds leaving Prague. "There was fresh money as some shifted from the Czech market," Czipo said.
Nevertheless, turnover was not particularly strong, with slightly over one million shares and compensation coupons trading.

"Most of the investors in central Europe are turning their eyes on problems in the Czech Republic," said James Oates, director for central and eastern Europe at UBS in London. "The crisis is getting much bigger."
"The result is that most people therefore are trying to change their positions in the Czech Republic and they are not really focusing on Hungary."
On Friday, the coupons gained the most in percentage term, adding almost seven percent to finish at 670 forints.

As for shares, the few losers included the less liquid papers but also retailer Fotex whose shareholders on Thursday decided to cancel two convertible bond issues to existing shareholders, planned for September 1997 and March 1998. Fotex ended at 140 forints, down five.
Elsewhere on the market, chemicals BorsodChem, rated by Hungary's OTP Securities as "hold" ended at 6,700 forints, up 120.
Despite Friday's gain, analysts said the market's outlook was flat.

"We can expect a fairly sideways, not very exciting market over the next week or so while people try to understand what has actually happened in Prague and later on they focus agains on Budapest," UBS's Oates said.
"There will be little activity from foreigners because they're going to be concerned about what's happening in Prague."
